counterexamples: Re-cut cancelled at closure un-cut an exit that was really cut. Sequence: X cuts K; K kills someone, so KillShield removes the spark and ExitWasCut stays true; the shield ends while K is still trailing; Y cuts K again less than eps before K's return (the R14 cross-tick case). EventResolver.CancelCutAtClosure set ExitWasCut = false, so the return came out unchased (Return.Chased false) and captured K's whole loop. That breaks 7.1 ('a return with ExitWasCut captures nothing, even if the spark was removed') and 7.2 ('its loop stays lost'). Reproduced at 30, 60 and 144 Hz by KillTraitsAuditTests.KillAudit_6_ACancelledReCutAtClosureDoesNotUncutAnExitThatWasCut(true) before the fix.
fixes_applied: Assets/Scripts/Core/Sim/PlayerState.cs: Spark gains `internal bool ExitWasCutBefore`, the exit's ExitWasCut just before this spark spawned. No public API change.

Assets/Scripts/Core/Sim/EventResolver.cs: StepCuts sets ExitWasCutBefore = victim.ExitWasCut when it creates the spark. CancelCutAtClosure now restores the flag (`p.ExitWasCut = spark.ExitWasCutBefore;`) instead of clearing it. Doc comment updated.
Assets/Scripts/Core/Sim/Simulation.cs: DebugForceCut sets ExitWasCutBefore the same way.

summary:
Section 7 does not fully hold as built: I found one real bug in the Core and fixed it with a few lines. Everything else I attacked held.

**The bug.** KillShield removes the spark from a chased killer but leaves its exit marked as cut, so its loop stays lost. After the shield ends, that exit can be cut a second time (this is kill-core's "reading to confirm"). If the second cut lands less than eps before the return, the R14 rule cancels it as a cut at closure. The old code then cleared the "exit was cut" flag, so the return captured the whole loop. The fix makes the spark remember the flag's value from before it spawned, and the cancellation restores that value. In classic rounds that value is always false, so nothing changes there.

**Classic is still bit-identical.**
- I built a fresh player into Build/kill-verify twice, the second time after the fix.
- Both builds print [ProbeHash] 246577239DE179C4 at -fps 30 and -fps 144. I looked at the screenshots and they render correctly.
- The probe still reports FAIL, but only because the europe package's EuropeMap shader lacks _PIO_ShaderId.
- In the Core, classic bot rounds never touch the new kill state, and every spark runs at exactly SparkSpeed.
- The three kill traits present but disabled (with invalid parameters) reproduce the rolling hash 8CB763231AC73608.

**Everything else held**, tested in Assets/Tests/EditMode/Core/KillTraitsAuditTests.cs (34 cases, all green):
- **Switchable and movable:** each kill trait put into each of the three biome sets (9 sets) is behaviour-only, deterministic, and identical to the plain biome set when switched off.
- **Kill attribution:** only the cut kept by R11 gets the kill (largest s_cut wins, ties go to the lowest index).
  - Two victims at once are both paid; the boost stacks to 1.2 and the shield starts once.
  - In a chain inside one group, only the killer alive after the group is paid.
  - A killer captured to death before its kill, or in the same group, gets nothing.
  - A chased killer keeps its inherited land until its own killer takes everything.
  - Losing your last cell to a capture never pays a reward.
- **KillInheritance:** with Share 0.5 and ScorchedEarth, the inherited core is never scorched and Propagation never fills the scorched rim. Propagation grows from inherited land in the same tick. A pending lasso pocket never lists cells the killer already owns. A kill in the time-up group still returns the trailing killer before the round ends.
- **KillSpeedBoost:** at 30 Hz the HeadGrace check uses the product of the speed maxima (0.338), and that step is actually reached. A cut in the same group as the victim's own kill gets a spark at 10.8 x 1.1.
- **KillShield:** a shield ending exactly on a tick boundary cuts at that instant at every rate. HeadGrace still applies at the shield end: a follower 0.4 u behind the head cuts at exactly the end, one 0.3 u behind never does. A catch of the killer within eps of its own kill is simultaneous, so the killer dies unpaid. A cut killer saved by the shield still loses its pending pocket.
- **Bot rounds:** an independent per-event checker ran on every tick of full rounds at 30, 60 and 144 Hz (all eleven traits, the three default biome sets, random kill parameters). It covered about 90 kills per rate, with every reward type paid. It also checked "spark speed fixed at the cut", "cuts stay outside HeadGrace" and "chased exactly when the exit was cut". Same-seed twin rounds gave identical hashes.

**Test runs:**
- dotnet: 554 of 554 pass on the final tree.
- Unity EditMode: 706 cases; 701 passed, 4 skipped (existing explicit fixtures) and 1 failed: liq-drop's WaveC_Composites_KeepTheirFetchCount, not mine. All 26 of my cases that run under Unity pass.

**Decisions and gaps for the user** (listed under contract_issues and needs in the report):
- The 7.1 sentence about the R14 cancellation needs amending to "restores the flag to its value before that spark".
- The user still has to confirm whether an exit can be cut again after a shield. With the fix, both answers stay consistent.
- KillSpeedBoost's Cap and Conduction's factor have no upper bound. At 30 Hz, accepted keys such as KillSpeedBoost(0.1,4) alone, or Conduction 1.3 with Cap 2.85, make round creation throw on the HeadGrace check.
- Kill traits can't yet be switched or moved in the game itself: the Runtime has no BiomeTraitTable and never sets the traits. Per-biome probes can't run until it does.
- kill-core owns PlayerState.cs, EventResolver.cs and Simulation.cs in this wave and should keep the fix when it next edits them.

The full report is at C:/Dev/squad-ai/Brainstorming/games/painter_io/docs/waveD/kill-verify.json. Probe logs and screenshots are in TestResults/kill-verify_probe_classic_fps30 and _fps144 (first build) and TestResults/kill-verify_probe_classic_fixed_fps30 and _fps144 (build with the fix).
